title: Top self-intersection under an arbitrary proper-variety morphism
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $X,Y$ be nonempty proper integral $k$-schemes of finite type of the same dimension $g\geq1$ [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a $k$-morphism and $\mathcal L$ an invertible module on $Y$ [def-sc-invertible-module]. In the intersection-number convention [def-sc-intersection-number],
$$((f^*\mathcal L)^g\cdot X)=\begin{cases}[k(X):f^*k(Y)](\mathcal L^g\cdot Y),&f\text{ dominant},\\0,&f\text{ not dominant}.\end{cases}$$
Here dominant means that the image is dense; in the dominant case the induced extension of function fields [def-sc-function-field] is finite. No finiteness of $f$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0BET, lemma-intersection-number-and-pullback, with Z=X and all entries equal; zero-image-dimension clause

proof.text:
The morphism $f$ is proper by [lemma-nagata-proper-to-separated-target], since $X$ is proper over $k$ and $Y$ is separated over $k$. $Y$ is Noetherian, being of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Put $\mathcal F_i=R^if_*\mathcal O_X$; by [lem-pc-coherent-hi] (proper $f$, Noetherian $Y$) every $\mathcal F_i$ is coherent and only finitely many are nonzero. For $\mathbf n=(n_1,\ldots,n_g)\in\mathbf Z^g$ put $\mathcal M(\mathbf n)=\bigotimes_{j=1}^g\mathcal L^{\otimes n_j}$; tensor powers with negative exponent mean powers of the inverse invertible module. Pullback commutes with these tensor products: on opens trivializing $\mathcal L$, the canonical tensor comparison is the identity on a free rank-one module, so it is an isomorphism and the comparisons glue; thus $f^*\mathcal M(\mathbf n)\cong\bigotimes_j(f^*\mathcal L)^{\otimes n_j}$. The same local calculation shows that the tensor powers and their pullbacks are invertible, so that $\mathcal G_{\mathbf n}=f^*\mathcal M(\mathbf n)$ is coherent on $X$. The Euler--Leray clause of [lem-pc-euler-additive] for the proper $k$-schemes $X,Y$ and $\mathcal G_{\mathbf n}$ gives $\chi(X,\mathcal G_{\mathbf n})=\sum_i(-1)^i\chi(Y,R^if_*\mathcal G_{\mathbf n})$. By [lem-pc-projection-formula] ($f$ is qcqs, $\mathcal O_X$ is quasi-coherent, $\mathcal M(\mathbf n)$ invertible), $Rf_*(\mathcal O_X)\otimes\mathcal M(\mathbf n)\cong Rf_*(f^*\mathcal M(\mathbf n))$. Tensoring with the locally free $\mathcal M(\mathbf n)$ is exact, so taking $i$-th cohomology sheaves gives $R^if_*\mathcal G_{\mathbf n}\cong\mathcal F_i\otimes\mathcal M(\mathbf n)$. Hence
$$P_X(\mathbf n):=\chi(X,\bigotimes_j(f^*\mathcal L)^{\otimes n_j})=\sum_i(-1)^i\chi(Y,\mathcal F_i\otimes\mathcal M(\mathbf n)),$$
a finite sum of Euler characteristics of coherent modules.

source.place: Tag 0BET, lemma-intersection-number-and-pullback, first displayed equality and the sentence after it (Lemma 0BEK and the projection formula Cohomology 01E8); coherence and finiteness as in the proof of Tag 0BEK (Tag 02O5)

proof.text: Suppose $f$ is not dominant. Put $Z=f(X)\subsetneq Y$. This set is closed because $f$ is proper, and is nonempty and irreducible because $X$ is nonempty and integral. On $V=Y\setminus Z$ the inverse image is empty, so [lem-pc-higher-direct-image-open-restriction] gives $\mathcal F_i|_V=0$ for every $i$. Thus every support is contained in $Z$. Any chain of irreducible closed subsets of $Z$ can be extended by the strict inclusion $Z\subsetneq Y$; therefore $\dim Z\leq g-1$ by [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. By [lem-sc-snapper-numerical-polynomial], each nonzero summand in step 1 has total degree at most $g-1$. Its coefficient of $n_1\cdots n_g$ is zero. The finite sum therefore has this coefficient zero. By [def-sc-intersection-number] this coefficient is $((f^*\mathcal L)^g\cdot X)$, proving the nondominant case.

Suppose $f$ is dominant. By [lem-sfb-equal-dimension-generic-structure-image], the actual extension $k(X)/f^*k(Y)$ is finite of degree $e$, there is a nonempty open $U\subseteq Y$ on which every $\mathcal F_i$ for $i>0$ vanishes, and $(\mathcal F_0)_{\eta_Y}=k(X)$ as a $k(Y)$-vector space. The supports of $\mathcal F_i$ for $i>0$ lie in the proper closed subset $Y\setminus U$. Every chain there extends by $Y$, so each has dimension at most $g-1$. By [lem-sc-snapper-numerical-polynomial], all positive-$i$ terms in step 1 have total degree less than $g$ and do not contribute to the coefficient of $n_1\cdots n_g$.

source.place: Tag 0BET, generic-image paragraph and higher-image lower-degree terms

proof.text:
The support of $\mathcal F_0$ is $Y$: it contains $\eta_Y$ by step 3, and a coherent module has closed support (locally a finite presentation gives a finite generating list; if its stalk is zero, finitely many neighbourhoods on which these generators vanish have a common open intersection). Since $Y$ is integral its only top-dimensional support component is $Y$ itself, with generic local ring $\mathcal O_{Y,\eta_Y}=k(Y)$. Its generic multiplicity is $e$: a basis of the finite-dimensional vector space $k(X)$ gives a filtration by spans with exactly $e$ one-dimensional simple successive quotients. Apply [lem-sc-numerical-polynomial-leading-term] to $\mathcal F_0$ and the $g$ entries all equal to $\mathcal L$. It gives
$$\chi(Y,\mathcal F_0\otimes\mathcal M(\mathbf n))-e\chi(Y,\mathcal M(\mathbf n))$$
of total degree less than $g$. With steps 1 and 3, the coefficient of $n_1\cdots n_g$ in $P_X$ is therefore $e$ times that in $\chi(Y,\mathcal M(\mathbf n))$. By [def-sc-intersection-number] these two coefficients are respectively $((f^*\mathcal L)^g\cdot X)$ and $(\mathcal L^g\cdot Y)$. This proves the dominant formula, including the asserted finiteness of the induced function-field extension.
